blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Around eighty per cent of tax problems come from a handful of recurring mistakes. Missed deadlines. Missing documentation. Wrong classification of a recurring expense. Confusing personal and business costs. Failing to update for a new rule announced months ago.

Preventing them is rarely about knowing more. It is about building small checks that catch each mistake before it happens: a calendar that flags deadlines two weeks in advance, a one-page classification guide that sits next to the expense form, and a monthly check that compares this quarter's rules with last quarter's, to catch anything the tax office quietly changed.

If we set up these simple checks, most of the errors that used to eat our time will stop happening on their own. The discipline is not heroic. It is just the habit of building small barriers exactly where the mistakes tend to fall.

items.q: According to the text, where do most tax problems come from?
items.why: "Around eighty per cent of tax problems come from a handful of recurring mistakes."

items.q: What does the text say prevention is mostly about?
options: Learning far more about tax law
Building small checks that catch mistakes early
items.why: "It is about building small checks that catch each mistake before it happens."

items.q: Why is the monthly check that compares quarters useful?
options: It speeds up the filing process
It catches rules the tax office quietly changed
It reduces the total tax owed
items.why: "a monthly check that compares this quarter's rules with last quarter's, to catch anything the tax office quietly changed."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Simple routines can prevent most errors
Fixing tax problems mainly requires deeper expertise
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que prevenir "raramente é sobre saber mais" — logo, o autor discordaria da ideia de que a solução é mais expertise.

items.q: By calling the discipline "not heroic", the author suggests that…
options: the mistakes are impossible to prevent
prevention is a modest, everyday habit rather than a dramatic effort
only senior staff can do this work
items.why: Inferência: "not heroic… just the habit of building small barriers" — é rotina simples, não um feito extraordinário.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte explicando as barreiras que está montando. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So I sat down last week and listed every tax mistake we made across the whole of last year. There were nine of them. And when I grouped them, they all fell into just three buckets. That surprised me — I expected the problems to be scattered everywhere.

The first bucket was deadlines. Twice we filed late simply because nobody was watching the calendar. So I've set up reminders that flag every deadline two weeks in advance, and they go to two people, not one.

The second bucket was classification. Three times we booked a recurring expense under the wrong category. My fix is a single-page guide that sits right next to the expense form, so the answer is there before anyone has to guess.

The third was the rules changing under our feet. The tax office updated a threshold in the spring and we simply missed it. Now, on the first Monday of every month, one of us compares this quarter's rules against last quarter's.

None of this is clever. But between them, these three checks would have caught every single mistake before it ever reached the return. That's the whole point — small barriers, exactly where we keep tripping.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many mistakes did Charlotte find, and into how many groups did they fall?
options: Three mistakes falling into nine buckets
Nine mistakes falling into nine buckets
Eighty mistakes falling into three buckets
Nine mistakes falling into three buckets
items.why: "There were nine of them… they all fell into just three buckets."

items.q: What is Charlotte's fix for the deadline problem?
options: Hiring an external firm to file for the team
Filing every return a month early
A monthly review of last quarter's rules
Reminders that flag each deadline two weeks in advance, sent to two people
items.why: "reminders that flag every deadline two weeks in advance, and they go to two people, not one."

items.q: What surprised Charlotte when she reviewed the mistakes?
options: There were far more than she expected
They grouped into just three buckets instead of being scattered
They were all caused by one person
None of them had reached the tax return
items.why: "That surprised me — I expected the problems to be scattered everywhere," mas caíram em só três grupos.

items.q: Why does Charlotte send the deadline reminders to two people rather than one?
options: To share the blame if a deadline is missed
Because the software requires two recipients
To train a replacement for the role
So the reminder still works even if one person overlooks it
items.why: Inferência: um dos erros foi "nobody was watching the calendar"; dois destinatários criam uma rede de segurança se um falhar.

items.q: What does Charlotte mean by "None of this is clever"?
options: She doubts the team will follow them
The checks are too simple to work
The solutions are ordinary, not sophisticated, yet effective
The mistakes were caused by clever fraud
items.why: Inferência: ela valoriza a simplicidade — "small barriers, exactly where we keep tripping" — não é engenhoso, mas resolve.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The same error kept coming back every quarter — a classic recurring mistake." A recurring mistake is…
options: a mistake made by a new employee
a one-off slip that never repeats
an error that keeps happening again and again
items.why: Recurring mistake = erro recorrente, que se repete.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We were fined because of a ___ — the return went in three days late."
items.why: Missed deadline = prazo perdido; a multa veio por atraso na entrega.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "The software booked the software licence under the wrong ___, so the totals were off."
items.why: Classification = classificação; a despesa foi categorizada errado.

items.q: "The reminder flags the payment two weeks in advance." In advance means…
options: ahead of time, before it is due
items.why: In advance = com antecedência, antes do prazo.

items.q: "We got caught because we failed to update our records for the new threshold." This means we…
options: shared the records with the wrong team
did not update the records when we should have
items.why: To fail to update = deixar de atualizar; não fizemos a atualização necessária.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em conversas sobre compliance e finanças. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Every recurring expense has to be signed off on by the finance lead." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new classification guide across all three offices next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The team agreed to the new checks but never followed through." They…
options: failed to carry them to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado — aqui, não levaram.

items.q: "We need to keep on top of rule changes so nothing slips past us." To keep on top of something means to…
options: ignore it until it becomes urgent
stay in control of it and up to date
items.why: Keep on top of = manter-se por dentro e no controle de algo.

items.q: "A late filing can easily slip through the cracks when no one owns the calendar." This means it can…
items.why: Slip through the cracks = passar despercebido, escapar sem ser notado.
